Felicity Party: Turkey. The Felicity Party (Turkish: Saadet Partisi, SAADET) is an Islamist political party in Turkey.

In which country did the Jeju uprising take place?

In which country was the Sultanate of Hobyo?
Sultanate of Hobyo: Somalia. It was established in either the 1870s or 1884 by Yusuf Ali Kenadid.

Habsburg monarchy: German. It became extinct in the male line in 1740, but continued through the female line as the House of Habsburg-Lorraine.

Delhi Sultanate: Persian. The sultanate was established in 1206 in the former Ghurid territories in India.

Marinid dynasty: Arabic. Although of Berber origin, the Marinid rulers were culturally Arabized.

Agape (from Ancient Greek (agp)) is "the highest form of love, charity" and "the love of God for and of for God".
Founded by a religious reformer recognized by his followers as the Mahdi, which Berber Muslim empire ruled much of the Maghreb and Islamic Spain from 1121 to 1269?
Almohad Caliphate was a North African empire ruled by a Berber Muslim dynasty in the 12th and 13th centuries that lasted from 1121-1269.
This Malaysian politician became his country's 10th prime minister in 2022 and promptly appointed himself finance minister as well — who is he?
Anwar Ibrahim (born 10 August 1947) is a Malaysian politician who has served as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia since 2022.

Fought in 937, this clash pitted King Æthelstan of England against an allied force led by the kings of Dublin, Scotland, and Strathclyde, and is sometimes called the birthplace of English national identity — which battle?
Battle of Brunanburh was fought in 937 between thelstan, King of England, and an alliance of Olaf Guthfrithson, King of Dublin; Constantine II, King of Scotland; and Owain, King of Strathclyde.
Named for the two censuses of the Israelites it records, this fourth part of the Torah opens at Mount Sinai just after the Law is given — which text?
Book of Numbers (from Greek, Arithmoi, lit. 'numbers') is the fourth book of the Hebrew Bible and the fourth of five books of the Jewish Torah.

This Belgian politician became his country's youngest development minister at age 31, later led a liberal party, served as prime minister, and then presided over the European Council from 2019 to 2024. Who is he?
Charles Michel (born 21 December 1975) is a Belgian politician who served as the president of the European Council from 2019 to 2024.
This Taiwanese businesswoman and former Merrill Lynch analyst became a Legislative Yuan member in 2022 and ran as Ko Wen-je's vice-presidential pick in Taiwan's 2024 election — who is she?
Cynthia Wu (pinyin: W Xnyng; Wade-; born 18 May 1978) is a Taiwanese businesswoman, politician, and former financial analyst.

This Argentine president, raised poor but politically active, wrote his most famous book — a critique of the strongman Juan Manuel de Rosas — while in exile in Chile, before later leading the country himself. Who was he?
Domingo Faustino Sarmiento (15 February 1811 - 11 September 1888) was President of Argentina from 1868 to 1874.
This American murderer served as a hitman for his uncle's crime ring during a string of Osage Nation killings, and was ultimately pardoned by Oklahoma's governor in 1966. Who is he?
Ernest Burkhart (September 11, 1892 - December 1, 1986) was an American murderer who participated in the Osage Indian murders as a hitman for his uncle William King Hale's crime ring.
This Haitian leader trained as a doctor fighting tropical disease before becoming president in 1957 and turning his rule increasingly autocratic — who is he?
François Duvalier (14 April 1907 - 21 April 1971), also known as Papa Doc, was a Haitian politician and physician who served as president of Haiti from 1957 until his death in 1971.

In November 1688 the Catholic King James II was deposed in favor of his daughter Mary II and her Dutch husband William of Orange — an event some historians call the last successful invasion of England. What is it called?

Glorious Revolution was the deposition of King James II in November 1688. The two ruled as joint monarchs of England, Scotland, and Ireland until Mary's death in 1694, when William became ruler in his own right.
Born and raised in New York, this politician moved to San Francisco in 1972, opened a camera store, and became the first openly gay man elected to public office in California — who is he?

Harvey Milk (May 22, 1930 - November 27, 1978) was an American politician and the first openly gay man to be elected to public office in California, as a member of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors.
A former Air Force commander, this leader stepped into Egypt's presidency after Anwar Sadat's 1981 assassination and held it for nearly thirty years until a revolution forced him out. Who was he?

Hosni Mubarak (4 May 1928 - 25 February 2020) was an Egyptian politician and military officer who served as the 4th president of Egypt from 1981 until his resignation in 2011, following the Egyptian revolution.
The only queen to reign in her own right over a unified Spain, this monarch took the throne a month before her third birthday in 1833 and was deposed in 1868 — who was she?
Isabella II (10 October 1830 - 9 April 1904) was Queen of Spain from 1833 until her deposition in 1868.
Nicknamed the Milwaukee Cannibal, this American serial killer murdered seventeen men and boys between 1978 and 1991, luring many victims to his Wisconsin apartment — who was he?

Jeffrey Dahmer (May 21, 1960 - November 28, 1994), also known as the Milwaukee Cannibal or the Milwaukee Monster, was an American serial killer and sex offender who killed and dismembered seventeen men and boys between 1978 and 1991.
This Spanish PSOE leader left office in December 2011 after pursuing peace talks with ETA and pushing through reforms to the country's autonomous statutes — who is he?
José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero (born 4 August 1960) is a Spanish politician and member of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE).
This Tamil and Telugu film star, now a politician, has taken home a Kalaimamani Award and a Kerala State Film Award across a 200-plus-film career — who is she?
Khushbu Sundar (born Nakhat Khan on 29 September 1970) is an Indian politician, actress, film producer and television personality.
The only president of Ukraine ever to serve two full terms, his 1994-to-2005 presidency brought economic stabilization but also scandal and the rise of powerful oligarchs — who was he?
Leonid Kuchma (born 9 August 1938) is a Ukrainian politician who served as the second president of Ukraine from 19 July 1994 to 23 January 2005.
At its greatest extent, this Javanese Hindu-Buddhist maritime empire's territory and tributary states spanned nearly the entire Indonesian archipelago — what's the historic empire?

Majapahit (Javanese) or (western dialect)), also known as Wilwatikta (Javanese), was a Javanese Hindu-Buddhist thalassocratic empire in Southeast Asia based on the island of Java (in modern-day Indonesia).

First elected to the Reichstag in 1903, this Centre Party politician turned against unrestricted submarine warfare and proposed a 1917 peace resolution before heading Germany's armistice delegation — who is he?
Matthias Erzberger (20 September 1875 - 26 August 1921) was a German Centre Party politician who served as the minister of finance of Germany from 1919 to 1920.

Born in 1942, this Republican has held the Senate seat from Kentucky since 1985 and was the longest-serving senator in the state's history. He served as Senate Republican leader for 18 years across three stints. Who is he?
Mitch McConnell (m-; born February 20, 1942) is an American Republican Party politician and attorney serving as the senior United States senator from Kentucky, a seat he has held since 1985.
This Salvadoran leader ran an advertising company before entering politics, served as mayor of San Salvador, and founded the Nuevas Ideas party after being ousted from the FMLN — who is he?
Nayib Bukele (born 24 July 1981) is a Salvadoran politician and businessman who has served as the 43rd president of El Salvador since 2019.
This Swedish politician led the Social Democratic Party and served as Prime Minister twice — 1969 to 1976, then 1982 until his assassination in 1986. Who was this Stockholm statesman?
Olof Palme (30 January 1927 - 28 February 1986) was a Swedish politician and statesman who served as Prime Minister of Sweden from 1969 to 1976 and 1982 to 1986.

A printer and War of 1812 militia lieutenant, this Whig was twice elected mayor of Washington D.C. while amassing one of the most extensive private collections of Revolution-era maps and manuscripts in America — who?
Peter Force (November 26, 1790 - January 23, 1868) was an American politician, newspaper editor, printer, archivist, and early American historian.
Built on the belief that inherited attributes make one group superior to another, this term also covers everyday prejudice against people of a different ethnic background. What is it?
Racism is the belief that groups of humans possess different behavioral traits corresponding to inherited attributes and can be divided based on the superiority of one race or ethnicity over another.
The eldest son of a US president, and the only one of his four siblings to live past 18, this lawyer served as Secretary of War and later as US Ambassador to Great Britain. Who was he?
Robert Todd Lincoln (August 1, 1843 - July 26, 1926) was an American lawyer and businessman.

Originally referring to inhabitants of ancient Arabia Petraea, this medieval European term evolved after the rise of Islam to become the standard Christian label for Muslims and the Muslim world broadly — what's the term?
Saracen was commonly used in medieval Europe to refer to a person who lived in or near what the ancient Romans knew as Arabia Petraea and Arabia Deserta.
Bordered by the Black Sea and wedged between the Soviet Union, Hungary, Yugoslavia, and Bulgaria, this Warsaw Pact communist state existed from 1947 until a 1989 revolution — what was it called?
Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period
Socialist Republic of Romania was a communist state that existed from 1947 to the Romanian revolution in 1989.
Before becoming director-general of the World Health Organization in 2017, this Ethiopian diplomat served as his country's minister of health and later minister of foreign affairs — who is he?

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus (Ge'ez:, sometimes spelled; born 3 March 1965) is an Ethiopian public health official, researcher, diplomat, and the director-general of the World Health Organization (WHO) since 2017.
Educated at Allahabad University, this Indian politician joined the Congress party in 1969 and later became prime minister for less than a year, from 1989 to 1990 — who is he?
V. P. Singh (25 June 1931 - 27 November 2008) was an Indian politician who served as the Prime Minister of India from 1989 to 1990 and the Raja Bahadur of Manda.

The leading German fighter ace of the Spanish Civil War, he became the first pilot in history to shoot down 100 enemy aircraft and devised the famous finger-four formation — only to die as a passenger in a plane crash. Who was this airman?
Werner Mölders (18 March 1913 - 22 November 1941) was a World War II German Luftwaffe pilot, wing commander, and the leading German fighter ace in the Spanish Civil War.
Ruling Uganda since 1986 and effectively banning political parties for nearly two decades, this former rebel leader is now among the world's longest-serving non-royal leaders — who is he?
Yoweri Museveni (born 15 September 1944) is a Ugandan politician, dictator, and former rebel leader who has served as the president of Uganda since 1986.
Succeeding his father Mahmud II in 1839, this mild-mannered Ottoman sultan launched the reforming Tanzimat era with an edict announced upon his accession — who was he?
Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha
Abdülmecid I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1839 to 1861.
Becoming Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister at age 38, this Samajwadi Party leader is the youngest person ever to hold that office — who is he?
Akhilesh Yadav: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh from 2012 to 2017.

Alfred Jodl: German general and war criminal (1890–1946)

Andrey Vlasov: Soviet Russian general and politician (1901–1946)
Born on Delos as the twin sister of Apollo, this Greek goddess presided over hunting, wild animals, and childbirth while herself remaining chaste — who is she?
Artemis: Ancient Greek goddess. In one account, Artemis is born first and then proceeds to assist Leto in the birth of the second twin, Apollo.
Raised at the Lakhmid court in al-Hira, this Sasanian King of Kings reportedly won his crown by snatching it after facing down two lions — earning the nickname 'Gur,' the onager hunter. Who was he?
Bahram V: Shahanshah of the Sasanian Empire from 420 to 438.
Which Pakistani leader became the first woman to head a democratic government in a Muslim-majority nation, serving two terms as prime minister before her assassination in 2007?
Benazir Bhutto: Prime Minister of Pakistan (1988–1990; 1993–1996)
This Russian physicist-turned-politician served as the first governor of Nizhny Novgorod Oblast before becoming an outspoken critic of Vladimir Putin — who was he?
Boris Nemtsov: Russian scientist, statesman, and politician (1959–2015)

Carlos the Jackal: Venezuelan-born international terror operative (born 1949)
The youngest mayor in the history of Taipei, this politician is the great-grandson of a former Nationalist Chinese president — who is he?
Chiang Wan-an: Taiwanese politician and lawyer (born 1978)

Constantine II of Scotland: King of Alba from 900 to 943.
According to the Hebrew Bible, this leader of the Tribe of Judah rose to become the second king of the united Kingdom of Israel — whose name means 'beloved one'?
David: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.

Founded in 1999 by Robert Fico as a splinter from Slovakia's post-communist left, this party has dominated Slovak politics since 2006 while blending left-wing economics with nationalist appeal — which party?
Direction – Social Democracy: Slovak political party. The party identifies as social-democratic, and was described as a combination of "leftist economics and nationalist appeal".
Nicknamed Longshanks and the 'Hammer of the Scots,' this English king who ruled from 1272 also held Gascony as a vassal of France — who was he?
Edward I: King of England from 1272 to 1307.
According to Genesis, this patriarch lived 365 years before God 'took him' rather than let him die, and tradition credits him as author of an apocryphal book bearing his name — who is he?
Enoch: Biblical figure prior to Noah's flood.
This Turkish engineer-turned-politician founded and leads an Islamist party that's the successor to one his father once led as Turkey's prime minister — who is he?
Taking the Habsburg throne in 1848 after his uncle's abdication, this long-reigning emperor saw his realm reconstituted in 1867 as the dual monarchy of Austria-Hungary — who was he?
Franz Joseph I: Habsburg monarch from 1848 to 1916.
Appointed by Stalin to lead the Soviet secret police from 1934 to 1936, this official oversaw the show trials of the Great Purge before becoming a victim of the very system he built — who is he?
Genrikh Yagoda: Soviet secret police official (1891–1938)
Fought across the 10th and 11th centuries, this series of conflicts pitted a Korean dynasty against the Liao dynasty of China — which conflict?
Goryeo–Khitan War: 10th and 11th century conflicts in Korea.
Developed through blending West and Central African beliefs with Catholicism, this religion teaches of a transcendent creator called Bondye and spirits known as lwa — what is it called?

Said by ancient tradition to have discovered the True Cross during a religious tour of Jerusalem, this Greek-born Augusta was canonized a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches — who was she?
Helena, mother of Constantine I: Roman empress and saint (c. 246–c. 330)
Considered the third person of the Trinity in Nicene Christianity, which concept represents God's animating presence across the Abrahamic faiths?
Holy Spirit: Religious concept with varied meanings.

The son of the labyrinth's architect, this figure from Greek myth escaped imprisonment on wings of feathers and wax, only to plunge into the sea after ignoring his father's warning not to fly too close to the sun — who was he?
Icarus: Greek mythological figure. Icarus and Daedalus escaped using wings Daedalus constructed from birds' molted feathers, threads from blankets, the leather straps from their sandals, and beeswax.
In this Islamic narration, Muhammad makes a night journey and ascends to the sky, glimpsing the afterlife before returning — alluded to in Surah al-Isra. What is it called?
Signs of the coming of Judgement Day
Isra' and Mi'raj: Journey by Muhammad in Islamic tradition.

Grand Hetman of Lithuania and one of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth's most celebrated commanders, he fought in the Wallachian, Polish–Swedish, Polish–Muscovite, and Polish–Ottoman wars — who is he?
Jan Karol Chodkiewicz: Polish–Lithuanian military leader (c. 1561 – 1621)

Born under a cloud of doubt about his parentage after his mother's captivity by a rival tribe, this early Mongol Empire prince became a military commander and the ancestor of the rulers of the Golden Horde — who is he?
Jochi: Mongol prince and general (c. 1182 – c. 1225)
Nicknamed 'Vinegar Joe,' this U.S. Army general commanded American forces in the China-Burma-India theater and became a war hero for leading his column out of Burma on foot in 1942. Who was he?
Joseph Stilwell: United States Army general (1883–1946)

This German physician-politician became a household name during the COVID-19 pandemic for his frequent talk-show appearances, before serving as the country's Federal Minister of Health from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
Karl Lauterbach: German scientist and politician, Federal Minister of Health, Member of the Bundestag.
A dependency of England and then Great Britain from 1542 to 1800, this island realm was administered from Dublin Castle by a Lord Lieutenant appointed by the English crown — what was it called?
Kingdom of Ireland: Dependency of England and then of Great Britain (1542–1800). The Parliament of Ireland was almost exclusively Anglo-Irish.
Founded in 2001 by brothers Jarosław and Lech Kaczyński, this Polish right-wing populist party won the 2005 presidential and parliamentary elections — which party?
Law and Justice: Right-wing and nationalist political party in Poland.
This Germanic people migrated south from near the Elbe river through the Danube region before conquering most of the Italian Peninsula between 568 and 774 AD — who were they?
Lombards: Historical ethnic group of the Italian Peninsula of Germanic origin.
Elected in 2020, this North Carolina congressman became the first member of Congress born in the 1990s, before controversies helped end his reelection bid in 2022 — who is he?
Twice queen consort of England through her marriage to Henry the Sixth, this daughter of the King of Naples personally led the Lancastrian side during the Wars of the Roses — who is she?
Margaret of Anjou: Queen of England (1445–1461, 1470–1471)
A brigadier general who led El Salvador through most of World War II, he served as the country's 27th president until resigning in 1944 — which Salvadoran officer?
Maximiliano Hernández Martínez: President of El Salvador from 1931 to 1934 and 1935 to 1944.
Twice shot in the head fighting the Turks and surviving both times, this Russian field marshal defeated Napoleon in 1812 through attrition warfare and earned the honorific 'of Smolensk' — who was he?
Mikhail Kutuzov: Field Marshal of the Russian Empire (1745–1813)
In Ovid's 'Metamorphoses,' this son of Somnus, the Roman god of sleep, visits mortals in their dreams disguised in human form — who is he?
Morpheus: Deity associated with sleep and dreams.
After two failed attempts in 1944, this Hindu nationalist activist shot Mahatma Gandhi three times at a Delhi prayer meeting in January 1948 — who was he?
Nathuram Godse: Assassin of Mahatma Gandhi (1910–1949)
Trained as a classical ballet instructor and educated in Czechoslovakia, this monarch ascended the Cambodian throne in 2004, just a week after his father's abdication — who is he?
Norodom Sihamoni: King of Cambodia since 2004.
This Austrian-born SS commando led the Gran Sasso raid that freed Mussolini from captivity and later advised Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser after fleeing to Franco's Spain — who was he?
This British explorer and his eldest son vanished in 1925 hunting an ancient lost city he was convinced lay hidden in the Amazon rainforest — who was he?
Percy Fawcett: British explorer and military officer.
Begun when reformer Alexander Dubček became First Secretary in January 1968, this period of liberalization in Czechoslovakia ended with a Warsaw Pact invasion that August — what is it called?

Prague Spring: Liberalisation in Czechoslovakia in 1968. The Prague Spring (Czech: Pražské jaro; Slovak: Pražská jar) was a period of political liberalization and mass protest in 
the Czechoslovak Socialist Republic.
This Indian politician became Minister of Defence in 2019 and was the first person born after independence to serve as Union Minister of Home Affairs — who is he?
Rajnath Singh: Defense Minister of India since 2019.
Going by his initials 'rms,' this programmer launched the GNU Project, founded the Free Software Foundation, and wrote every version of the GNU General Public License — who is he?
Richard Stallman: American activist and programmer (born 1953)
Orphaned of his murdered father at age two, this Shia cleric grew up to lead a revolution that toppled the Shah and made him his country's first supreme leader — who was he?
Ruhollah Khomeini: Supreme Leader of Iran from 1979 to 1989.
Leader of Spain's far-right Vox party since 2014 and president of Patriots.eu since 2024, this politician represents Madrid in the Congress of Deputies — who is he?
Lord of the desert and god of storms and chaos in ancient Egyptian religion, he murdered his own brother Osiris before being pursued for revenge by his nephew Horus — who is this god?
Set (deity): Egyptian god of the desert, storms, violence, and foreigners.
Ruling from 893 to 927, this monarch's campaigns against the Byzantines and Magyars brought the First Bulgarian Empire to its greatest size and a cultural Golden Age — who was he?
Simeon I of Bulgaria: First Emperor of the Bulgars from 893 to 927.

Born in Trinidad, this civil rights leader helped launch the Black Power movement while heading SNCC, then served as 'Honorary Prime Minister' of the Black Panther Party — and later took the name Kwame Ture. Who was he?
This Umayyad commander crossed from North Africa to launch the Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula in 711, leaving his name forever attached to the rock where he massed his troops — who is he?
Tariq ibn Ziyad: Umayyad commander in Hispania (died c. 720)
Coregent with his stepmother Hatshepsut for 22 years before ruling alone, this pharaoh led between 17 and 20 victorious military campaigns that brought Egypt's empire to its peak — who is he?
Thutmose III: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1479 to 1425 BC.

Born in Ohio and originally named Hiram, this West Point graduate led the Vicksburg campaign that seized control of the Mississippi River before becoming the Union's top general and eventually the 18th U.S. president — who is he?
Ulysses S. Grant: Civil War general, U.S. president from 1869 to 1877.
A former central bank governor who tamed hyperinflation, he became Ukraine's third president in 2005 on a platform of turning the country toward the EU and NATO. Who is he?
Viktor Yushchenko: President of Ukraine from 2005 to 2010.

Named after the city where its constitution was drafted, this German state of 1918 to 1933 marked the country's first constitutional experiment of its kind — a label later coined by Hitler in 1929 — what was it called?
Weimar Republic: German state from 1918 to 1933. The state was officially named the German Reich; but was more commonly referred to, and unofficially proclaimed itself, as the German Republic.
Elected tsar of Russia by the Seven Boyars in 1610 — though he never took that throne — this eldest son of Sigismund III went on to rule Poland and Lithuania; who is he?
Władysław IV Vasa: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania from 1632 to 1648.
China's premier through the 1980s, he was the architect of political reform — until his support for the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests cost him all his power. Who is this fallen reformer?
Who among these was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
C++ (founded 1983) is the earliest of the four. C++ is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Danish computer scientist Bjarne Stroustrup.
Which of these is an astronomer?
Nancy Roman is an astronomer. Nancy Grace Roman (May 16, 1925 – December 25, 2018) was an American astronomer who made important contributions to stellar classification and stellar motions.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Isaac Newton is a mathematician. Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
What is the atomic number of Tantalum?
Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
What is the atomic number of Copper?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
In what year did Neil Armstrong die?
Neil Armstrong: Armstrong was born and raised near Wapakoneta, Ohio.
In what year was Methylphenidate discovered?
Methylphenidate: It may be taken by mouth or applied to the skin, and different formulations have varying durations of effect.
Which company manufactures TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkish Aerospace Industries. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Chromium: Pfizer. Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrus?
Hydrus: Petrus Plancius. Hydrus is a small constellation in the deep southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Tiktaalik?
Tiktaalik: Neil H. Shubin. Tiktaalik is estimated to have had a total length of 1.25–2.75 metres (4.1–9.0 ft) on the basis of various specimens.
Who is credited with discovering Fluoxetine?
Fluoxetine: David T. Wong. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
Who is credited with discovering HTML?
HTML: Tim Berners-Lee. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
In chemistry, this class is defined by an −OH group that lends water-loving properties to otherwise water-shy hydrocarbons, spanning everything from ethanol to sugar versions — what is it?
Alcohol (chemistry) (from Arabic al-kul 'the kohl') is a type of organic compound that carries at least one hydroxyl (OH) functional group bound to a saturated carbon atom.
This deep-tissue swelling — of the face, tongue, throat, or limbs — comes on within minutes to hours and is driven by either histamine or bradykinin — what is it?
Angioedema is an area of swelling (edema) of the lower layer of skin and tissue just under the skin or mucous membranes.
Jointed legs, a chitin exoskeleton they must moult to grow, and haemolymph instead of blood mark which wildly diverse group of invertebrates?
Arthropod are invertebrates in the phylum Arthropoda.
Not contagious and believed to be partly genetic, this multi-system inflammatory condition can also cause blood clots, aneurysms, or blindness in severe cases — which condition?
Behçet's disease (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
Recognised by South Africa's Kennel Union but not by the international federation, this large, muscular mastiff-type breed serves as a family guard dog — name it?
Boerboel is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
This general-purpose, multi-paradigm programming language was designed at Microsoft by Anders Hejlsberg and first widely released in 2000, later becoming an international standard. What is it?
C Sharp (programming language) is a general-purpose high-level programming language supporting multiple paradigms.
This neuropsychiatric syndrome, often linked to mood or psychotic disorders, can leave a person nearly motionless for days or cause repetitive, purposeless movements. What is it?
Catatonia is a neuropsychiatric syndrome most commonly seen in people with underlying mood disorders such as major depressive disorder, or psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia.
This insect family, known as the 'true' members of its group, contains roughly 3,400 species worldwide, distinct from just two species in a smaller sister family. What family is it?

Cicadidae is one of two families of cicadas, with about 3,400 species in over 520 genera worldwide; it contains most living cicada species, except for the two belonging to its sister taxon, the Tettigarctidae.

Often called the most renowned Greek mathematician since antiquity, he spent his career in Germany advancing measure theory and the calculus of variations — and even built an axiomatic formulation of thermodynamics. Who was he?
Constantin Carathéodory (13 September 1873 - 2 February 1950) was a Greek mathematician who spent most of his professional career in Germany.
This American biologist, who later ran Caltech and founded the Whitehead Institute, won a Nobel at just 37 for discovering the enzyme reverse transcriptase. Who was he?
David Baltimore (March 7, 1938 - September 6, 2025) was an American biologist, university administrator, and 1975 Nobel laureate in Physiology or Medicine.
Charles Darwin spent years experimenting on these mucilage-coated plants, first proving that plants could be carnivorous — which genus of nearly 200 "sundew" species is it?
Drosera is commonly known as the sundews, is one of the largest genera of carnivorous plants, with at least 194 species.
This inflammation of the small intestine is most often caused by contaminated food or drink, though NSAIDs, radiation, and autoimmune conditions can also trigger it. What is it?
Enteritis is inflammation of the small intestine. Duodenitis, jejunitis, and ileitis are subtypes of enteritis which are localised to a specific part of the small intestine.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Its name comes from Greek for 'milk flower,' and this small genus of about 20 bulbous perennials nods with a single white bell of six tepals — what is the botanical name for the snowdrop?
Galanthus (from Ancient Greek, (gla, "milk") + (nthos, "flower")), or snowdrop, is a small genus of approximately 20 species of bulbous perennial herbaceous plants in the family Amaryllidaceae.
This system of rules governs how a language is structured, covering everything from word order to the deeper study of sounds, meaning, and sentence formation — what is it called?
Grammar is the system of rules that governs how a natural language is structured and used, as evidenced by its speakers or writers.
Living to the age of 104, this French pioneer of algebraic topology was also the son-in-law of physicist Pierre Weiss and the eldest of a remarkable scientific brood — who was he?
Henri Cartan (8 July 1904 - 13 August 2008) was a French mathematician who made substantial contributions to algebraic topology.
Classified under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5, this condition causes a lack of alertness during waking hours despite — or because of — too much sleep. What is it?
Hypersomnia is a neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness.
This medical condition describes a restricted blood supply to tissue or an organ, starving cells of the oxygen they need and often resulting from a blocked or narrowed vessel — what is it called?
Ischemia is a restriction in blood supply to any tissue, muscle group, or organ of the body.
Born in Los Angeles to South Korean immigrant parents, this NASA astronaut and physician previously served as a Navy SEAL on over 100 combat missions — who is he?
Jonny Kim (born 5 February 1984) is an American NASA astronaut, physician, U.S.

Sold under a well-known brand name, this medication treats several types of epilepsy including focal and tonic-clonic seizures, and also helps stabilize mood by reducing future depressive episodes in bipolar disorder — which drug?
Lamotrigine (luh-), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
This Chinese computer engineer turned science-fiction writer won the 2015 Hugo Award for his novel The Three-Body Problem, and has also claimed China's Galaxy Award a record nine times. Who is he?
Liu Cixin (pinyin: Li Cxn,; born 23 June 1963) is a Chinese computer engineer and science fiction writer.

Living from about 6.2 million years ago until roughly 4,000 years ago, this extinct relative of modern elephants is distinguished by its large, spirally twisted tusks and cold-weather adaptations like a thick fur coat — name the animal?
Mammoth is a member of the extinct elephantid genus Mammuthus.

This cluster of at least three conditions -- including high blood sugar, high triglycerides, and low 'good' cholesterol -- raises heart disease and diabetes risk in roughly a quarter of American adults. What is it called?

Metabolic syndrome is a clustering of at least three of the following five medical conditions: abdominal obesity, high blood pressure, high blood sugar, high serum triglycerides, and low serum high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
Found naturally in the dark resin of opium and given everywhere from pills to spinal injections, this opiate alters how the brain feels pain — what is it?
Morphine is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Found across North America, Europe, North Africa, and Asia, this three-stage amphibian passes through an aquatic larval phase and a land-dwelling 'eft' stage before adulthood — what is it?
Newt is a salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.
Fossils of these arachnids in 400-million-year-old Scottish rock look startlingly modern — colloquially they're called harvestmen or daddy long legs. What order is this?
Opiliones (formerly Phalangida) are an order of arachnids, colloquially known as harvestmen, harvesters, daddy long legs, or granddaddy long legs.

One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory — the study of when order must inevitably appear — and cracked countless open problems across number theory and combinatorics; who was he?
Paul Erdős (26 March 1913 - 20 September 1996) was a Hungarian mathematician known as one of the most prolific mathematicians and producers of mathematical conjectures of the 20th century.

Derived from phosphoric acid by removing one to three protons, this anion or salt takes forms like dihydrogen and hydrogen variants and gives its name to fertilizers and various esters — name the ion?
Phosphate is an anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.

Attacks of this condition — abdominal pain, vomiting, and confusion lasting days to weeks — stem from a buildup of porphyrins and can be triggered by stress, smoking, or certain medications. What is it?
Porphyria (or) is a group of disorders in which substances called porphyrins build up in the body, adversely affecting the skin or nervous system.
Easily identified by its striking red and black coloring, this common European insect is often mistaken for an unrelated lookalike called the cinnamon bug — what insect is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.
Beyond his Nobel-winning work in quantum electrodynamics, he explained the superfluidity of supercooled liquid helium and built the parton model — which physicist?
Richard Feynman (May 11, 1918 - February 15, 1988) was an American theoretical physicist.
Milder than most of its Allium relatives like garlic and leeks, this vegetable has a long, hollow green stem and no fully developed bulb — what is it commonly called?
Scallion (also known as green onions and spring onions) are edible vegetables of various species in the genus Allium.
This spiny thistle species has distinctive red-to-purple flowers and shiny, pale green mottled leaves, and is a fairly typical member of the daisy family — what plant is it?
Silybum marianum is a species of thistle.
Haunted by the Holocaust and the Eichmann trial, this American social psychologist ran his notorious obedience experiments in a Yale basement in 1961. Who was he?
Stanley Milgram (August 15, 1933 - December 20, 1984) was an American social psychologist who conducted controversial experiments on obedience in the 1960s during his professorship at Yale.

Named after a figure from Greek mythology condemned to eternal frustration, this hard, corrosion-resistant blue-gray metal, atomic number 73, is mined alongside the chemically similar niobium in the ore known as coltan. What element is this?
Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.

Founding pastor of Redeemer Presbyterian Church in New York City and co-founder of Redeemer City to City, this American theologian wrote the bestsellers The Reason for God and The Prodigal God — who was he?
Tim Keller (pastor) (September 23, 1950 - May 19, 2023) was an American Presbyterian pastor, Reformed theologian, and Christian apologist.
Medically called micturition or voiding, this voluntary process happens up to seven times a day in a healthy adult — and goes by "number one." What is it?
Urination is the release of urine from the bladder through the urethra in placental mammals, or through the cloaca in other vertebrates.
This small insect-eating songbird breeds across most of Europe and Asia, migrates to Africa in winter, and has a black-backed form that predominates in Britain and Ireland — what is it?
White wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws.
This Andalusi polymath built a model of the planets' motion, devised colourless glass, made reading lenses, and is even said to have attempted flight — who was this 9th-century inventor?
Abbas ibn Firnas: 9th-century astronomer and physician.
People with this anxiety disorder dread places they feel they can't safely escape — crowds, queues, public transit — and in severe cases become unable to leave home at all. What is it?
Agoraphobia: Anxiety disorder. Agoraphobia is believed to be due to a combination of genetic and environmental factors.

Believed to be an autoimmune attack on the immune privilege of hair follicles, this condition typically leaves a few coin-sized bald spots — and in rare cases takes every hair on the body. What's it called?
Alopecia areata: Medical condition. Alopecia areata (AA), also known as spot baldness, is a condition in which hair is lost from some or all areas of the body.
Google's open-source mobile operating system, built for touchscreen phones and tablets, runs on a modified version of which kernel?

Android is an open-source operating system developed by Google, based on a modified version of the Linux kernel and other free and open-source software, designed primarily for touchscreen mobile devices.

Named from a Tupi word imitating the sound these macaws make, this genus of large, vividly colored Neotropical parrots includes eight living species prized — and poached — for the pet trade — which genus?
Ara (bird): Neotropical genus of macaws. Ara is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.
Found from the Labrador Sea to the Barents Sea and able to live up to 25 years, this widely eaten fish can occasionally top 180 centimeters and 50 kilograms — what species is it?
Atlantic cod: Species of fish. The Atlantic cod (pl.: cod; Gadus morhua) is a fish of the family Gadidae, widely consumed by humans.

Members of the family Ursidae walk flat on plantigrade paws tipped with five claws that can't retract — and though most eat meat, the giant panda among them is mostly herbivorous. What animal is this?
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Unlike benzodiazepines, this anti-anxiety medication doesn't cause sedation or dependence, and works through serotonin 5-HT1A receptors with a delayed onset of two to four weeks — which drug?
Buspirone: Medication used to treat anxiety disorders.
Domesticated in Mexico roughly 6,000 years ago, this nightshade produces berries used in cooking, medicine, and even self-defense sprays — which plant species is it?
Capsicum annuum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Originally called 'centigrade' from Latin words for a hundred and steps, this SI temperature scale was renamed in 1948 to honor the Swedish astronomer who proposed it in 1742 — which scale?
Celsius: Unit of measurement for temperature.

The second-lightest halogen, this yellow-green gas is so reactive it has the highest electron affinity of any element and once fascinated medieval alchemists heating chloride salts — which element is it?
Chlorine: Chemical element with atomic number 17 (Cl)
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?

This physical law holds that within an isolated system, nothing is created or destroyed — only transformed, as when a stick of dynamite converts stored chemical potential into heat, sound, and motion — what law is it?
Conservation of energy: Law of physics and chemistry.
Squash, pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, and the plant behind loofah sponges all belong to which family, nicknamed the gourds?
Cucurbitaceae: Family of plants. The Cucurbitaceae ( kew-KUR-bih-TAY-see-ee), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
In psychiatry, this is a fixed false belief that persists even in the face of clear contradicting evidence, commonly seen in schizophrenia and manic episodes of bipolar disorder — what is it?
Delusion: Fixation of holding false beliefs.
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.
In 1990, this theoretical physicist became the first physicist ever awarded the Fields Medal, later becoming known as the practical founder of M-theory — who is he?
Edward Witten: American theoretical physicist. Witten is a researcher in string theory, quantum gravity, supersymmetric quantum field theories, and other areas of mathematical physics.
Serving as chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, which ancient Greek polymath was the first known person to calculate Earth's circumference?
Eratosthenes: Greek librarian, mathematician, geographer, and poet.
Powerfully built with a small head, stocky body, and a coat of black, white, brown, and grey, this is the only species of its kind still living in the UK — what is it?
European badger: Species of mustelid. It is classified as least concern on the IUCN Red List due to its wide range and large, stable population size which is thought to be increasing in some regions.
When fibroblasts overproduce collagen after repeated injury or chronic inflammation, this permanent connective-tissue scarring can impair an organ's normal function — what is it called?
Fibrosis: Excess connective tissue in healing.
Native from the British Isles east to the Caucasus, this tree in the olive family is prized for wood that's flexible, strong, and lightweight — what is its scientific name?
Fraxinus excelsior: Species of deciduous tree.
Deriving its name from Greek words for 'earth' and 'study of', this branch of natural science examines rocks and the processes that have shaped the planet over time — what is it called?
Geology: Scientific study of Earth's physical composition.
This waterfowl family member is smaller than a swan but larger than a duck; its young are called goslings, and a flock on the ground is known as a gaggle — what bird is it?
Goose: Common name for a group of waterfowl.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is prized smoked as Finnan haddie or the Arbroath smokie — what fish is it?
Haddock: Species of fish. The haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.

Many people show no symptoms after catching this liver-attacking virus, but when signs do appear weeks later they can include nausea, yellowing skin, and fatigue — and an infection lasting past six months is deemed chronic. What is it?

Drawing on anthropology, paleontology and genetics, this field studies how our species gradually gained bipedalism, dexterity and complex language — and shows our past was weblike, with interbreeding among archaic humans — what is the subject?
Human evolution: Homo sapiens is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.

Named from the Greek word for "fish" because of its dry, scaly skin, this family of genetic skin disorders ranges from a mild type mistaken for ordinary dry skin to a rare, life-threatening form — which condition?
Ichthyosis: Family of disorders causing dry, thickened, scaly skin.
This purplish-black Brazilian fruit doesn't dangle from branches — it sprouts straight out of the tree trunk itself. What is it?
Jabuticaba: Tree in the family Myrtaceae.
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
Sold under names like Toradol and Acular, this NSAID's use is capped at five days due to serious side-effect risk, with relief starting within an hour — what drug is it?
Soft, dense, and bluish-silver when freshly cut, this heavy metal carries the highest atomic number of any stable element — and its Latin name, plumbum, gives it the symbol Pb. Which element is it?
Lead: Chemical element with atomic number 82 (Pb)
Element number 3, this soft silvery-white alkali metal is the least dense metal of all and so reactive it must be stored under oil or in an inert atmosphere — what is it?
Lithium: Chemical element with atomic number 3 (Li)
A Russian linguist by training, this woman served two separate terms as first lady of Russia, from 2000 to 2008 and again from 2012 to 2014 — who is she?
Lyudmila Putina: Ex-wife of Vladimir Putin (born 1958)
The first Mexican-born scientist to win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, this physical chemist shared the 1995 award for revealing how CFC gases threaten the ozone layer — who?
This mammal family — skunks and stink badgers — was reclassified out of the weasel family in the 1990s after genetic evidence, and turns out to be closest kin to red pandas and raccoons. What is it?
Mephitidae: Family of mammals. In taxonomic order, the living species of Mephitidae are:.

Codenamed 'Havoc' by NATO, this Soviet tandem-seat attack helicopter carries a single gun in an under-nose barbette and, unlike its predecessor, has no secondary troop-transport role. What aircraft is this?
Mil Mi-28: Russian attack helicopter. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.
Forming dense green mats with leaves just one cell thick, these seedless plants reproduce via spore-topped stalks called sporophytes — which plants?
Moss: Division of typically non-vascular land plants.
The sole surviving family of an ancient cephalopod lineage, these nine living species carry coiled chambered shells 10 to 25 cm across and are all protected under CITES — what creatures are they?
Nautilus: Family of molluscs. It comprises nine living species in two genera, the type of which is the genus Nautilus.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and spread by the fecal-oral route, this is the most common cause of gastroenteritis — what is it?
Norovirus: Type of viruses that cause gastroenteritis.
Named after an ancient Greek city, this cactus genus is better known by its fruit's common name, the prickly pear, and goes by nopal or sabra in other cultures — what genus is it?
Opuntia: Genus of cactus. The plant has been introduced to Australia, southern Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Africa.
One researcher catalogued as many as 549 varieties of this psychological category, defined by intense arousal toward things that aren't sexual by nature — what is the term?
This serous membrane lines the abdominal cavity and serves as a conduit for the blood vessels and nerves of the organs it covers — what is it called?
Peritoneum: Membrane that forms lining of abdominal cavity or coelom.
Scientifically named Cajanus cajan, this perennial Fabaceae legume is a staple crop across the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean — what is it?
Pigeon pea: Species of perennial legume. The pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) is a perennial legume from the family Fabaceae native to the Eastern Hemisphere.
Though they look like dolphins, these small toothed whales are actually closer kin to narwhals and belugas, with flat spade-shaped teeth instead of dolphins' cone-shaped ones — what are they called?
Porpoise: Small cetacean of the family Phocoenidae.

Found in more than 200 species of mushroom, this tryptamine alkaloid is itself biologically inactive — the body must dephosphorylate it into psilocin before the euphoria and time-bending kick in. What is it?
Psilocybin: Chemical compound found in some species of mushrooms.
Flying aboard Soyuz T-11 in April 1984 as part of the Soviet Interkosmos programme, who became the first citizen of his country to reach outer space?
Rakesh Sharma: First Indian to travel to space (born 1949)
He shared the 1965 Nobel for quantum electrodynamics and dreamed up a now-famous pictorial shorthand for the behavior of subatomic particles — which physicist lent his name to those diagrams?
About 500 times sweeter than table sugar but prone to a bitter, metallic aftertaste, this odorless artificial sweetener also goes by the additive code E954 — what is it?

Native to the North Pacific coastline, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, and one of few animals known to use rocks as tools to crack open shells — what is it?
Sea otter: Species of marine mammal. The sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Highly water-soluble and non-hygroscopic, this colorless compound with formula AgNO3 is the least expensive salt of its kind — which compound?
Silver nitrate: Chemical compound. It is highly water soluble colorless solid that is a precursor to many other silver compounds.
Combining vowel and consonant sounds into words for acts like persuading or declaring, this use of the human voice can even happen without any listener at all — what is it?
Speech: Human vocal communication using spoken language.
A bitter, colorless alkaloid from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, it kills birds and rodents by triggering muscular convulsions and asphyxia. Which poison is it?
Strychnine: Poisonous substance used as pesticide.
Known by folk names like bitter buttons and golden buttons, this Eurasian flowering plant in the daisy family has become invasive after being introduced to Australia and the Americas — which plant?
Tansy: Species of plant. Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare) is a perennial, herbaceous flowering plant in the genus Tanacetum in the family Asteraceae, native to temperate Europe and Asia.

Its severe, chronic form is called beriberi — a name possibly borrowed from a Sinhalese phrase meaning "I cannot, I cannot," for the weakness it causes; a shortage of which vitamin (B1) is the culprit?
Caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii and often spread through undercooked meat or infected cat feces, this disease is famously dangerous to catch during pregnancy — what is it?
Normally containing two arteries and one vein cushioned in Wharton's jelly, this conduit links a developing fetus to the placenta — what is it?
Umbilical cord: Conduit between embryo/fetus and the placenta.
This Russian-Canadian programmer co-founded Bitcoin Magazine in 2011 before deploying a rival blockchain platform in 2015 alongside Gavin Wood and Charles Hoskinson — who is he?
Also called sallows or osiers, this genus of roughly 350 mostly deciduous tree and shrub species thrives on moist soil in cold, temperate regions — which plant?
Americium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for americium is Am. Americium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Am and atomic number 95.
The symbol for flerovium is Fl. Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.

Aishwarya Rai: Rai won the Miss World 1994 pageant and later established herself as one of the most-popular and influential celebrities in India.
